messages:
alex_support: @lina_oncall customer (ACME corp) opened a ticket: sudden 502/504 spike against hosted inference endpoints in us-east-1 starting ~11:10 UTC. They see Envoy upstream resets and partial streams. Provided a few request IDs: req=8a2f1c3b, 8a2f2d4e. Sample curl they ran below.

sam_sre: Can you paste the curl and any x-request-id/trace headers? also which model/route?

alex_support: Route: POST /v1/generate (model: redwood-medium). curl: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` They attached one response (502) with body: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers".

lina_oncall: saw a similar blip in infra dashboard — h2 stream resets and Envoy "upstream reset" metric spiked on the edge gateways at the same minute. Could be h2 windowing or auth-tier overload.

ajay_eng: Quick check: any recent config pushes to edge or auth proxy? deploy-bot: (deploy-bot) edge-config v2026.03.10 rolled at 10:58 UTC to 12 pods in us-east-1.

nate_api: Customer also mentioned they send a custom header set (X-Customer-Attrs) with large base64 payloads per request. That could affect header bytes and HPACK/serialization.

alex_support: Attached from customer: header dump snippet: ```X-Customer-Attrs: eyJ0ZW5hbnQiOiAiYWNtZS1wcm9qZWN0IiwgInVwIjo... (6kB)``` they said issue happens when they start a burst of parallel requests (~200 concurrent connections) from multiple hosts.

iris_prodops: Hypothesis: auth-cache misses + large headers cause auth backend (auth-tier) to do upstream lookups, increasing latency; Envoy gives up on upstream and resets streams -> 502/504. Also large headers can trigger upstream buffer/window drift.

sam_sre: Repro attempt — I ran a small script to open 150 concurrent HTTP/2 connections with a large header and did see increased `upstream_reset_before_response` and a few 502s within minutes. Script (pseudo): ```python
# open many h2 connections in a loop, send small payload and large X-Customer-Attrs header
```

ajay_eng: Noticed error lines from auth-proxy logs around the same time: `auth_cache: miss, fetching token for tenant acme, latency=520ms` combined with `upstream conn limit reached` on the edge.

lina_oncall: Immediate mitigations applied: bumped edge keepalive pool size + disabled HTTP/1->HTTP/2 multiplexing for that worker pool, and temporarily increased auth-cache TTL for the tenant. This dropped 502s to near zero in the next 5 minutes. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Customer confirmed reduced errors after the mitigation. They still want root cause and a permanent fix. They asked about white-labelling header sizes — can we advise limits?

ajay_eng: Action items: 1) auth team to add more aggressive caching for high-throughput tenants (short term TTL bump), 2) edge team to add header-size metric on gateways and fail-fast on grossly oversized headers, 3) consider serializing large attributes into object store + small pointer header.

nate_api: Also opening a quick regression check against the config roll that went out at 10:58; maybe an envoy change tightened buffer/window defaults. I'll diff the envoy bootstrap templates.

iris_prodops: For support reply: ask customer for: repro script (we have partial), list of headers per request, exact concurrency and client HTTP/2 settings (keepalives, connection reuse). Provide short-term workaround: reduce concurrency, shorten header payloads, or contact us to route them to a warmed dedicated pool while we stabilize.

sam_sre: Logging note: capture `edge_gateway/h2_stream_resets` alongside `auth_cache/latency` for next 24h. Also correlate with config-change timeline.

alex_support: I'll send the mitigation steps + asks to ACME and request the repro script and full header dumps. Marking ticket P1 until we have stable root-cause.

lina_oncall: If we confirm header serialization interacting with recent envoy defaults, patch candidate: increase per-stream window and add header_size guard. Planning canary on a single colo tomorrow.

ajay_eng: Filing a follow-up infra task and tagging the config roll suspects. I'll paste diffs when ready.

alex_support: thanks everyone — closing the internal thread, moving to the support ticket with the recommended mitigations and next steps. (reaction :eyes:)
